summary: Both parts come from the adapted real point g that defines zeroTermFin: (i) zeroTerm ∘ ω(g) maps the spanning translates of the vacuum into the finite part of V₀; (ii) the Heisenberg action moves to the finite datum, and the real zero-term law for g gives the real datum v₀.

steps.claim: Let g be the chosen real point adapted to D (Splitting.exists_isAdapted_and_frame_eq with t = 1) that defines zeroTermFin, and h the statement that it is adapted.
By IsAdapted.mixedTerm_omega_vacElem there is c ≠ 0 with (ω(g)vac)[x] = c·|e(x)|²·vac₀ in the mixed model; this fact is put in the context for the automation below.

(i): for f in 𝒲_f(V), zeroTermFin(D)f = zeroTerm_D(ω(g)f′) with f′ = ω(1, g_f⁻¹)f again in the finite part (finite-part vectors are fixed by the real projection, and ω of finite points preserves 𝒲_f); zeroTerm_D ∘ ω(g) sends the spanning vectors ϱ_f(x)vac of 𝒲_f(V) into 𝒲_f(V₀), hence the whole span (map_span_le).
steps.lean:
use fun f hf ↦ ((D.zeroTerm ∘L V.ω g).1.map_span_le ..).2
    (by aesop (add simp [rho_finVec_mem_finitePart, finHeisOp,
    ω_ϱ])) ⟨_, omega_mem_finitePart g.2⁻¹ (projReal_of_mem_finitePart hf ▸ hf), by simp [g]⟩,

steps.claim: (ii): ϱ(y)(v ⊗ f) = w ⊗ ϱ_f(y_f)f for a real datum w (Space.exists_rho_integrated_eq). Writing w ⊗ F = ω(g)((ω(g⁻¹)w) ⊗ F′) (Space.omega_integrated) and applying the real zero-term law of the adapted g (IsAdapted.exists_real_zeroTerm, for the mixed law of the zero term) gives zeroTerm_D(w ⊗ ϱ_f(y_f)f) = v₀ ⊗ zeroTermFin(D)(ϱ_f(y_f)f) with v₀ the image of ω(g⁻¹)w under a bounded map L between the Fock spaces.
steps.lean:
(V.exists_rho_integrated_eq · · |>.imp' _ fun w e f ↦ by simpa [e, g] using
    (V.omega_integrated g⁻¹ w _ ▸ (h.exists_real_zeroTerm D.isMixedLaw_mixedTerm).choose_spec .. :))
